title: A uniformly discrete counterexample to bounded approximation in Lipschitz-free spaces

issues.description: The nonlinear corollary depends on a paraphrase of Kalton's net characterization (Kalton12, Thm 4.4): a single Lipschitz bound Λ for maps N_X→N_X with relatively compact range that approximate any finite set. The paper does not quote the exact hypotheses, for example whether the maps are Lipschitz or only coarse-Lipschitz. On a 1-separated net the two are equivalent up to constants, so the step probably holds, but it was not checked against the source. This affects only the side corollary, not Theorem 1.1.
issues.evidence: 'If X were approximable, Kalton's theorem would give one Lipschitz bound Λ≥1 for maps g:N_X→N_X with relatively compact range that approximate any prescribed finite subset as closely as desired.'

coverage:
Read every section in full: introduction, reduction, blocks, operators, walks, tests. Checked each step of the main proof chain:
- Wedge metric and the reduction by retraction and inclusion (P_p U I_p has norm ≤ λ ≤ p).
- Direct proof of AP via R_N = Σ I_p P_p.
- ℓ1 coefficient isomorphism with the bounds 1/2 and B, and the 2B-BAP.
- Finite-support perturbation (η < 1/(2B) gives anchor error < 1 and norm < 2p).
- Signed-measure total-variation bound V = 1 + 4pB, using a sign test function with Lipschitz constant ≤ 2.
- Bump mass ≥ 3L/4, using (2pR+1)/K ≤ 1/5. Sympy confirms 1/5 − (2pR+1)/K = (2p−1)/(10p(30p+1)) ≥ 0, and B = 300p² + 150p + 5.
- Local-limit lemma: permutation model plus a second-moment argument.
- Block geometry: label map is 1-Lipschitz, the radius-2L ball bound Q, the color bound H, d(x,a) ≥ R.
- Rare matched walks: the event is determined by the radius-n ball, and a tree union bound gives |S|(H/k)(ΔQH/k)^n.
- Exceptional-direction record lemma, including loops, parallel edges and bad vertices.
- Edge-test Lipschitz verification: cross pairs at distance < 2L both vanish because the compatibility threshold is K+2L+1 = D−4. McShane extension plus clipping.
- Incidence averaging: E[loss] < 1/10, so the lower bound 11p contradicts the upper bound 2p.
- Order of quantifiers: graph sequence fixed, then T and S, then n and m.
No gap found. I did not verify the exact statement of the cited Kalton theorem used for the nonlinear corollary.
main_claim: There is a countable, unbounded, uniformly discrete (d ≥ 1) metric space M whose Lipschitz-free space F(M) has AP but fails λ-BAP for every λ. It is built as a wedge of bounded blocks M_p. In each block, every finite-rank operator of norm ≤ p has error ≥ 1/2 at some point of a fixed finite anchor set. As corollaries, real ℓ1 has an equivalent norm failing MAP, and F(M) is not approximable in Kalton's nonlinear sense.
